new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work is listed for koro1304, so a two-work spot-check of silent works is not possible; the one work was read in full and is genuinely silent on stress. As an extra check I re-a full-text search for stress/accent the prior check's Connell 2021 text (same folder): stress/accent/prominence/prosody 0 hits, tone 7 hits (p. 409 'Nominal forms and their allomorphs have no inherent tone, but bear the same tone as the stem'; polar tone on AGR), confirming the claim that Connell is tone-marked but silent on word stress. Nothing missed.

tone_statements.citation: Connell, Bruce. 2021. The gender system of Durop. STUF - Language Typology and Universals 74(2): 405-425. doi:10.1515/stuf-2021-1039 (green-OA repository copy, HU Berlin edoc)
tone_statements.quote: Nominal forms and their allomorphs have no inherent tone, but bear the same tone as the stem. [p.409] ... Numerals agree with the noun following the pattern of PROX DEM. Exceptions are found with NF NV- and BV- which, rather than the expected AGR markers ne-, be-, take instead na-, ba-. Rather than a falling tone, as for DEM, the AGR tone is polar to the preceding tone, and also copied to the numeral itself. [p.412] ... Associative constructions may involve tone changes on the second noun; these too are independent of agreement patterns. [p.413]
tone_statements.locator: p. 409 (sect. 2.1, before Table 1); p. 412 (sect. 2.2.2.2 'Agreement in numerals'); p. 413 (sect. 2.2.2.4)

sources.note: Native-speaker primer in a devised orthography; Ch.1 'Alphabet' lists letters only, no tone or stress section; in-volume search 'stress' 0 hits, 'tone' 0 hits. p.75 lay remark: positive vs negative forms spelled alike 'are differentiated by accents, with the positive ones having theirs on the first consonant and the negative ones on the last consonant, e.g. "'biabi" (bad) becomes "bia'bi" (not bad)'; pp.66-67 gloss individual verbs 'with accent on..'. Not a word-stress rule.

tone.says: Publisher description only ('sixteen chapters which address important elements of grammar, with some including mini bilingual dictionaries.. organised thematically'), written by a native speaker who is not a trained linguist (Decker et al. 2022: 380); Okon & Noah 2018 fault his earlier dictionary for 'the absence of phonetic transcription', so a tone analysis is unlikely, though an alphabet/pronunciation chapter may state whether tone is marked.

sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Treats Durop as tonal: all data tone-marked (H, L, falling, rising); p.409 'Nominal forms and their allomorphs have no inherent tone, but bear the same tone as the stem'; p.412 AGR tone 'polar to the preceding tone'; p.406-407 reduced ATR harmony. p.406: 'The only available linguistic study of Durop is Kastelein's (1994) unpublished undergraduate thesis.'

tone.quote: Nominal forms and their allomorphs have no inherent tone, but bear the same tone as the stem. [p.409] ... Numerals agree with the noun following the pattern of PROX DEM. Exceptions are found with NF NV- and BV- which, rather than the expected AGR markers ne-, be-, take instead na-, ba-. Rather than a falling tone, as for DEM, the AGR tone is polar to the preceding tone, and also copied to the numeral itself. [p.412] ... Associative constructions may involve tone changes on the second noun; these too are independent of agreement patterns. [p.413]
tone.locator: p. 409 (sect. 2.1, before Table 1); p. 412 (sect. 2.2.2.2 'Agreement in numerals'); p. 413 (sect. 2.2.2.4)
tone.says: No tone-inventory statement, but treats Durop as a tone language throughout: all forms carry H (acute), L (grave) and falling (circumflex) marks, incl. on long vowels; noun-class prefixes have no inherent tone and copy the stem tone (p.409); the proximal demonstrative AGR marker bears a falling tone while numeral AGR tone is polar to the preceding tone (p.412); associative constructions may involve tone changes on the second noun (p.413). Nothing on stress or accent. States that Kastelein 1994…
